claims.statement: The app defines three build types: debug (no minification, `.debug` applicationId suffix plus a `-debug` versionName suffix so it installs alongside release, full ABI set for emulators), release (R8 minification + resource shrinking, `arm64-v8a` only, `resConfigs("zh", "en")`), and benchmark (created via `initWith(getByName("release"))`, debug-signed, `isDebuggable = false`, adding `x86_64` ABI on top of release's arm64-v8a, `matchingFallbacks` to release).

Release builds ship arm64-v8a only (minSdk 33 devices are all 64-bit) and restrict resources to `resConfigs("zh", "en")`, enabling R8 minification plus resource shrinking with `proguard-android-optimize.txt`; the audit records the resulting release APK at ~6.2 MB. debug/benchmark keep multiple ABIs for emulator compatibility.

Release signing reads the gitignored `keystore.properties` (storeFile/storePassword/keyAlias/keyPassword); when it is missing, local builds fall back to debug signing with a warning, but passing `-PrequireReleaseSigning=true` (release/CI scenario) makes the build fail outright to prevent shipping a debug-signed "release" artifact.

The `check` lifecycle task aggregates root-level `spotlessCheck` and `verifyProductArchitecture` plus every subproject's `check`; each subproject's `check` also depends on its own `spotlessCheck`, so a full `check` runs formatting, architecture assertions, and all module unit tests across debug/release/benchmark variants.

`verifyProductArchitecture` is orchestration in the root `build.gradle.kts` `doLast` block whose rule body was extracted (m-10, 2026-10-15 review) into the `buildSrc` object `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.verify.ProductArchitectureVerification`: `verify(rootDir)` walks kt/kts/java/xml/toml files (skipping build/.gradle/.git/.idea AND buildSrc to avoid self-trigger from rule-text counterexamples), collects ALL violations into a LinkedHashSet, and the task throws one `GradleException` with the joined list (collection-style, not fail-fast). The rule behavior is unit-tested by `ProductArchitectureVerificationTest` with temp-directory repo fixtures (collection without abort, the `loadSongInfoSafely` exemption, brace-balanced `release` extraction); there is still no incremental or allowlist mode, so any new file/module enters the next scan.

The gate enforces the product module inventory and per-module hygiene: all 15 modules (including `:core:skin` and `:benchmark`) must appear in `settings.gradle.kts`, and every module directory must keep a local `.gitignore` containing `/build/`, `/.cxx/`, `/.externalNativeBuild/`, and `/captures/`.

Hilt assembly points are hard-gated: `MelodyApplication` (`@HiltAndroidApp`), `MainActivity` (`@AndroidEntryPoint`), `AppMediaSessionService` in :player (`@AndroidEntryPoint`), and `PlayerViewModel` (`@HiltViewModel`) must exist with their annotations, and the six required SingletonComponent Hilt modules (app/di: CoroutineModule, LoggerModule, PlayerModule; data/di: RepositoryModule, DatabaseModule, DataStoreModule) must exist as `@Module @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)` objects.

The gate pins the architecture docs: `docs/architecture/PLAYBACK_STATE_MACHINE.md` must exist and document the playback state/sync terms (idle..error states plus AppMediaSessionService, PlaybackController, ControllerPlaybackStateSynchronizer, PlayerControllerStateFacade, PlayerMediaEventFacade), and `docs/refactor/PRODUCT_REFACTOR_AUDIT.md` must track Verified / Still Not Fully Proven sections plus the release, benchmark, and test validation commands.

The gate locks the :benchmark module shape: the build file must use the Android test plugin, `targetProjectPath = ":app"`, and depend on `androidx.benchmark.macro.junit4`; `StartupBenchmark` must keep MacrobenchmarkRule, StartupTimingMetric, StartupMode.COLD, startActivityAndWait, and `packageName = "cn.com.dcsgo.mihx"`.

Performance observability is gate-anchored: `PerformanceTrace` must exist in :core:common, `MusicRepository` must keep the `music_import_scan`/`music_import_folder` trace operations, `PlaybackController` must keep `controller_play_queue`/`controller_prepare_queue`/`controller_sync_queue`/`play_next_command`, and `PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest` must keep covering the 100/500/1000-song queue sizes with the 71-item window bound.

Historical regressions are banned at source-scan level: no references to the legacy `com.dcsgo.data.model` package, no `PlayerViewModelComponents`/`PlayerViewModelComponentFactory` (the old manual assembly hub, deliberately replaced by PlayerRuntime and injected facade/graph objects; build.gradle.kts files that merely mention the names are skipped), and no Android Things dependency strings.

Module dependency boundaries are gate-enforced: feature build files must not declare `project(":data")`, `project(":player")`, or any `project(":feature:…")`; feature/domain/player sources must not import `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.(repository|local).*`; MusicRepository must not declare the four domain repository interfaces as supertypes while the four `*RepositoryAdapter.kt` files must exist and implement them; and the whole `:player` module (kt/java/xml) must not reference the stale `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player` package since its classes moved to `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.player` (matching the module namespace) — this rule prevents regression to the old implementation package.

UI routing patterns are gate-enforced: features must expose Route+Screen composables (lyrics, settings, play stats, quick-skip, version management are individually checked), the overlay routing files (AppOverlay.kt/AppOverlayHost.kt/OverlayRoute.kt) must not reappear, :feature:home must not import `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.ui.lyrics` directly, and :core:model must contain no res XML and no UI resource id references.

Privacy-sensitive capability startup is gate-enforced: Bluetooth monitoring must never initialize at app startup (PlayerStartupFacade must not contain `Bluetooth`, and the four startup-path files must not request notification/Bluetooth permissions); SettingsScreen must expose the user-triggered Bluetooth controls; and Bluetooth playback monitoring and playback notification must be persisted PlayerSettingsRepository/DataStore keys surfaced through PlayerUiState rather than app-shell local remember state, with PermissionCoordinator supporting onGranted callbacks.

Two product-wide code quality rules are machine-enforced: LazyColumn `items`/`itemsIndexed` calls in app/core/feature must declare a stable `key` within 160 characters (bare `item { }` is banned), and direct `android.util.Log` calls are banned everywhere except `AppLogger.kt` itself — all logging goes through AppLog/AppLogger.

Manifest placement rules are gate-enforced: `AppMediaSessionService` must be declared by the :player manifest (never the :app manifest), and the :app manifest must not declare READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE; READ_MEDIA_AUDIO is the one allowed exception so an already-granted device can fast-scan via java.io.File, with SAF document-tree access remaining the primary path and fallback.

The gate parses the app release build type by brace-pairing, not the old first-closing-brace regex: `extractBracedBlock(appBuildText, "release")` counts `{`/`}` and returns the balanced block (fixing the review-named truncation when nested lambdas appear), then requires `isMinifyEnabled = true` and `isShrinkResources = true` plus the `create("benchmark")` / `initWith(getByName("release"))` pair. The signing decision is deliberately kept outside `buildTypes` via a `releaseSigningConfig` val and the release block holds only flat assignments (`signingConfig = releaseSigningConfig`, `isMinifyEnabled`, `isShrinkResources`, `proguardFiles(...)`, `ndk { abiFilters += "arm64-v8a" }`) — although the comment above `buildTypes` still cites the old regex-truncation rationale.

Privacy/backup exclusion is a gate-enforced release checklist: both `backup_rules.xml` (full-backup-content) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer) must exclude the hard subset — the legacy SharedPreferences files (`music_player_prefs.xml`, `play_stats_prefs.xml`, `quick_skip_songs_prefs.xml`), the full melody.db family (db/journal/shm/wal), `datastore/player_settings.preferences_pb` + `datastore/playback_state.preferences_pb`, and `cache/album_art/`; adding a new persisted file requires updating both rule files or the architecture check fails.

Room schema JSONs are immutable snapshots whose version history is tamper-evident: schema v1 must not contain `quick_skip_short_play_counts`, v2 must contain it but not `lrcUri`, v3 must contain `lrcUri`. Since m-4 the migration objects live in `data/.../local/migration/MelodyMigrations.kt` (public, so the migration regression test references the same instances as production): the gate requires it to register `Migration(1, 2)` and `Migration(2, 3)` and `DatabaseModule` to call `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`; later schema versions and migrations are not gate-checked.

The Room schema workflow: :data exports schemas via `ksp { arg("room.schemaLocation", "$projectDir/schemas") }` and `MelodyDatabase` declares `version = 20, exportSchema = true`, with historical snapshots in `data/schemas/cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.local.MelodyDatabase/1.json…20.json`. The migration chain holds 19 migrations (`MIGRATION_1_2` … `MIGRATION_19_20`) in the trailing `ALL: Array<Migration>` array of `MelodyMigrations` (declared last so object properties initialize in order), registered by `DatabaseModule` via `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`; recent steps are v17 (`index_songs_albumId`, `index_playback_events_songId`), v18 (`songs.bitDepth`), v19 (bitRateKbps/channelCount/audioCodec/spatialAudio) and v20 (`MIGRATION_19_20` deletes all `song_group_overrides` rows because the groupKey semantics changed in 2026-11). Entity/DAO changes require an exported-schema bump, a `:data` build so KSP writes the new JSON (the `merge*UnitTestAssets` tasks depend on `ksp*variant*Kotlin` so `MigrationTestHelper` reads the fresh JSON), a new `Migration(N, N+1)` appended to `ALL`, a focused Robolectric migration test, and never hand-editing an already-exported schema JSON.

The :benchmark module provides three Macrobenchmark entry points: StartupBenchmark (two cold-start tests — StartupTimingMetric, 5 iterations each — comparing CompilationMode.None() vs CompilationMode.Partial(Require) via pressHome()+startActivityAndWait), ScrollBenchmark (FrameTimingMetric, 5 iterations, 3 down + 3 up home-screen swipes), and BaselineProfileGenerator (BaselineProfileRule.collect that writes app/src/main/baselineProfiles/baseline-prof.txt); it suppresses the EMULATOR error via testInstrumentationRunnerArguments and enables only the benchmark build type via androidComponents.beforeVariants.

Baseline Profile operations: the bundled baseline-prof.txt (~2425 rules, generated on a Pixel 6 emulator) is packaged into release builds and installed by androidx.profileinstaller to speed cold start and first-screen scroll; regeneration happens by running the `:benchmark` `BaselineProfileGenerator` on a real device/emulator (`:benchmark:connectedCheck`) — not via the non-existent `:app:generateBaselineProfile` task — with MIUI ROMs potentially blocking macrobenchmark's automated permission/frame-confirmation steps and physical-device cold-start acceptance still pending (emulator median ~810 ms, software-rendered).

PerformanceTrace is an explicit observability policy, not a logging side effect: `isEnabled` initializes from BuildConfig.DEBUG so debug builds trace everything while release is intentionally silent, an `allow`/`disallow` allowlist lets critical operations emit traces in release, and as of M-20 (2026-10-27) traces flow through the dedicated `AppLog.performance` channel (not `AppLog.info`), which `AndroidAppLogger` gates by the independent `performanceLoggingEnabled` flag rather than by BuildConfig.DEBUG — so release allowlisted operations genuinely reach the platform log; `measure`/`log`/`logLazy` emit through AppLog.performance with redacted metadata and only construct metadata when the trace will be output, and core/common explicitly enables buildConfig for BuildConfig.DEBUG.

AppLog/AppLogger is the only logging channel: `AndroidAppLogger` gates debug/info/warning behind the `debugLoggingEnabled` flag (= `BuildConfig.DEBUG`) while `error` always emits — but `error` appends the throwable stack trace only when debug logging is enabled, so a release crash log carries the redacted message line without the stack. Every message and stack trace passes through `redactSensitiveValuesForLog()` (content:// URIs, file:// URIs, Bluetooth MACs, device names, Windows/POSIX paths replaced with placeholders), so release builds expose only sanitized error logs plus allowlisted performance traces; the dedicated `performance(tag, message)` channel is gated by the independent `performanceLoggingEnabled` flag (default false for the no-op test delegate, opened true in `MelodyApplication` and `LoggerModule`) so release-allowlisted ops emit. `AppLog.install(AndroidAppLogger(BuildConfig.DEBUG, performanceLoggingEnabled = true))` runs in `MelodyApplication.onCreate`, and the uncaught-exception hook also logs through `AppLog`.

Version compatibility constraints: Kotlin 2.0.21 requires the built-in compose compiler plugin (`org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose`) and forbids the old `composeOptions { kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion }` block; KSP 2.0.21-1.0.28 must prefix-match the Kotlin version exactly; Media3 1.9.0 pairs with the Jellyfin FFmpeg extension 1.9.0+1; Room 2.6.1, Hilt 2.52, DataStore 1.1.1, AGP 8.13.2, Compose BOM 2025.09.01, minSdk 33 / compileSdk+targetSdk 36 with Java 11 bytecode; LiteRT 1.4.1 / WorkManager 2.9.1 / Coroutines 1.9.0 / Spotless 6.25.0 / Robolectric 4.14.1; effective versionName is 3.15.0 / versionCode 54 and the Room database is at schema v20. `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml` are the authoritative sources; the retired CLAUDE.md Key Versions table is historical only.

R8 keep rules in app/proguard-rules.pro preserve manifest entry points (MelodyApplication, MainActivity, AppMediaSessionService), Hilt/Room/Media3 reflection attributes, MelodyDatabase and entity classes for diagnosability, and the Jellyfin FFmpeg decoder classes (`FfmpegAudioDecoder`, `FfmpegLibrary`) because `:player`'s `FfmpegPcmDecoder` (now at `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.player`) drives the package-private Media3 FFmpeg decoder reflectively via a `Class.forName`-based `FfmpegLibraryProbe` — renaming or stripping these breaks the FFmpeg decode path. (The keep rule still lists the AppMediaSessionService name under the legacy `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player` FQN.)

Deterministic Windows verification depends on `kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process`: the Kotlin daemon used to fail creating client marker files on Windows and fall back mid-build, so compilation runs inside the Gradle daemon — which means `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx2048m` is the effective compile heap (`kotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx1536m` only applies out-of-process), alongside `org.gradle.parallel=true` and `org.gradle.caching=true`.

`android.nonTransitiveRClass=true` scopes each module's R class to its own declared resources, so resources must not be referenced across module boundaries via R classes — complementary to the gate rule that :core:model may carry no UI resource ids (mapping belongs in :core:ui or the owning feature, e.g. PlayMode.iconRes()).

Spotless is the formatting gate and must stay catalog-managed: the root build applies `alias(libs.plugins.spotless)` and defines kotlin/kotlinGradle/androidXml format rules (trim trailing whitespace, end with newline), the catalog must keep the spotless plugin entry, and both the root and each subproject's `check` must depend on `spotlessCheck` (both facts gate-enforced).

Device-dependent validation commands: `:app:connectedAndroidTest` (Compose instrumentation) and `:benchmark:connectedCheck` (macrobenchmarks including Baseline Profile generation) require a real device or emulator, whereas full `test` runs on the JVM across debug/release/benchmark unit-test variants; media-key/service behavior and the ActivityResult permission path are still verified primarily through JVM planner/facade/policy tests rather than end-to-end device tests.

OpenWiki pages are generated artifacts refreshed on demand; hand-editing them is discouraged — source code and tests are authoritative (per AGENTS.md), architecture facts belong in docs/ (several are gate-locked by verifyProductArchitecture), and `docs/README.md` routes build/test/architecture conventions to the openwiki pages. Two GitHub Actions workflows exist: `pr-check.yml` (pull requests + pushes to main, ignoring docs/**, openwiki/**, **.md, with a conservative version-only fast path) and `release.yml` (v* tags / workflow_dispatch) — release.yml re-runs the full `./gradlew check :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :buildSrc:test` gate on the commit being released (assembleDebugAndroidTest compiles instrumentation sources without a device; :buildSrc:test covers the gate rule body), then builds the signed APK, apksigner-verifies it, and publishes a GitHub Release.

The `:app` manifest's `<application>` sets `android:largeHeap="true"` (declared in v3.11.0), and release ships only `arm64-v8a` via `ndk.abiFilters` with `resConfigs("zh", "en")` trimming dependency-library translation resources; because minSdk is 33 all real devices are 64-bit.

The `pr-check.yml` and `release.yml` `check` jobs run `./gradlew check :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :buildSrc:test --no-daemon --stacktrace` on ubuntu-24.04 with JDK 17 (temurin); `:app:assembleDebugAndroidTest` only compiles the instrumentation test sources (no device, catching UI signature drift) and `:buildSrc:test` unit-tests the verifyProductArchitecture rule body.

Room v11 (versionCode 46 / versionName 3.11.0) migration adds the `word_preferences` emotion-word listening-preference voting table (`word` TEXT PRIMARY KEY, `likeVotes`/`dislikeVotes`/`updatedAt` INTEGER) via `MIGRATION_10_11`, backed by `WordPreferenceEntity` with `@Entity(tableName = "word_preferences")`.

The verifyProductArchitecture gate (buildSrc object `ProductArchitectureVerification`, driven by the root `verifyProductArchitecture` task) machine-enforces two code-shape rules from the 2026-10-27 wave: a `runBlocking` ban across all `src/main` sources (comment lines are ignored and trailing `//` comments stripped before matching, so historical prose about `runBlocking` does not trip it), and a ratchet banning `import android.*` in `:core:model`/`:domain` main sources that grandfathers the 5 pre-existing violations (`AlbumEntry.kt`, `ArtistEntry.kt`, `Song.kt`, `FolderImporter.kt`, `MusicImportRepository.kt`) via a baseline whitelist until the Uri→String migration clears them (androidx.compose.runtime.{Stable,Immutable} are exempt).

The gate bans bare `loadSongInfo(` calls in any `src/main` source outside `core/ui/.../SongInfoLoader.kt`: every call site must go through `:core:ui`'s `loadSongInfoSafely`, because an uncaught Room exception inside a `LaunchedEffect`/`produceState` coroutine previously propagated to the main-thread handler and crashed the process (C-1 fix, 2026-10-27); the rule and its exemption are covered by `ProductArchitectureVerificationTest`.

The gate requires at least one real `PerformanceTrace.allow(` call site in `src/main` (registered at startup in `MelodyApplication.onCreate` for the core playback operations), because `allow()` only decides whether a trace is computed while output goes through the independent `AppLog.performance` channel — without a call site the release allowlist API would be dead code (M-20 / gate suggestion 4).

`pr-check.yml` skips its heavy steps only for a conservative single-commit version bump: the fast path applies to `push` events whose `before`/`after` commits both exist locally (hence `fetch-depth: 0`), whose changed-file set is exactly `app/build.gradle.kts`, and whose every added/removed line matches `versionCode =` or `versionName =`. Pull requests, new branches/force pushes (zero `before`), multi-commit or mixed-file pushes, and any edit beyond those two lines run the full check; because the fast path exists, `release.yml` re-runs the whole `check` job on the commit being released.

`CLAUDE.md` is now a 5-line `OPENWIKI` stub that only points at `AGENTS.md`, so its historical build/architecture prose is no longer authoritative; current conventions come from the Gradle files (`app/build.gradle.kts`, root `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `gradle.properties`), the `buildSrc` gate body, `.github/workflows/`, `AGENTS.md` (source and tests authoritative, narrowest quiet validation, don't hand-edit generated OpenWiki pages) and `docs/` — whose `docs/README.md` index explicitly routes build/test/architecture conventions to the openwiki pages.

Baseline Profile regeneration runs through the `:benchmark` module's `BaselineProfileGenerator` (`BaselineProfileRule.collect`) on a device or emulator, i.e. via `:benchmark:connectedCheck`, which rewrites `app/src/main/baselineProfiles/baseline-prof.txt`; the current build applies no baseline-profile Gradle plugin, so the `:app:generateBaselineProfile` command mentioned in the generator's KDoc has no corresponding task in this repository.
